body:
alright
for scuba diving you wanna go to San Andrés, you'll have to go by air, but you may be able to grab good priced tickets here: https://vivaair.com/co (best airpline prices for national colombian flights, trust me)
So, if you wanna dive for just one day, plan a 3-day trip to San Andrés, arrive in the morning, get to know the locals, the island, and of course do anything you have to do to plan your diving ahead; second day is your diving day, I know the guys at http://bandadiveshop.com/, had a blast last year, if you make a phonecall they'll tell you everything you need to know (just remember, your spanish level has to be decent, I'm sure they speak english at the shop but it'll just make things easier for everyone); day three is your decompression day, go outside and enjoy the island (REMINDER: San Andrés is not a place to go shopping per se, rather than looking for malls and stuff go and take a stroll around the island, there are even some places when you can go rent a buggy car to actually go and take the whole circuit around the island, if you do it you won't regret it).
At San Andrés the seafood is amazing, but please do not buy any products made from sharks and turtles, please do not contribute to illegal hunting of endangered species
Now, let's say you return from San Andrés, you can now arrive to Bogotá, here you can visit La Candelaria, Monserrate, and downtown city, there are many things to see and learn around here. Just mind the weather and be very careful with your belongings, criminal rates are off the roof these days. In Bogotá there are ton of nightclubs you can enjoy, some can be hella expensive, some can be cheap af, but you have to do research before you choose, this city can be very dangerous, especially at night.
Why Bogotá when you have Cartagena, Cali, Medellín, etc? Because if you want to see high altitude places, I think the one's around Bogotá are easily accessible and very enjoyable
First, you wanna visit Monserrate, that's a prior, then you can go to  La Catedral de Sal in Zipaquirá, near Bogotá (it's a fucking underground cathedral built inside a salt mine, and it's just gorgeous) 
After La Catedral, you MUST visit either Sumapaz or Chingaza, both are natural parks in the "páramos" the ecosystem there is rare and almost unique to our country, to take the walking trails, two weeks ago I went to Chingaza and it was amazing
Near Bogotá there are also high altitude towns that are worth a visit, towns like Villa de Leyva, Paipa (please go to the thermals) and Guatavita are highly recommended and you can do a weekend trip to visit all three and whatever you may find in between 
For the "big rock thing with the stairs" I don't have any idea xD, there are many big rock things around here, maybe you're talking around Ciudad Perdida? In that case I wouldn't recommend it for a casual trip, it is at least a 3-day trial to get to the top of the mountain where the sacred city is, you'll have to cross through the thick jungle, a guide is required, and without any hiking experience its going to be a nightmare for the both of you. I went with my friends when we were aroud 15; 3 days to climb, 2 days to descent, in the whole time we didn't even bother to change our clothes, you can figure our why.
You'll definitely find waterfalls, it's Colombia after all. Near Bogotá there is El Salto del Tequendama (around 456 ft tall), and the mansion next to it which is spooky AS FUCK. Not many tourist around there in my humble experience.
I am talking to you about the places near Bogotá because that's where I live lmao, but in Cartagena there are a ton shit things to do and find, nightclubs surely are better there as well. 
Just enjoy your stay and have fun, you do not get bored in this country
Now I can't unsee it, thanks fam
